newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on overseas buying.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended up on Thursday compared with New York's previous close on overseas buying and some physical demand, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$337.80/338.30 on Thursday compared to New York's close at US$337.10/60 on Wednesday.
"We saw some Japanese buying in the morning," said one dealer.
Others said Japanese buying had boosted prices but Swiss selling had pushed the market slightly lower in the afternoon.
"It's a very mixed situation," said one dealer.
Physical demand had provided some support to prices but, with the local tael exchange carry over charge at about eight percent, punters buying gold would have to pay interest.
"If the tael interest rate remains at -8.00, people will continue to sell tael and buy loco London," said one senior dealer.
Trade was said quiet with few players willing to take fresh positions before the long holiday when markets in Hong Kong will be closed for the territory's handover to China on July 1.
The market was also awaiting the over-the-counter options expiry later on Thursday in the hope of fresh direction which would take gold beyond its current tight range of $337.00 to $339.00.
Local tael gold ended HK$3 lower at HK$3,130.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous fix at -8.00.
